),

)

  g,
  r,
  i,
  z,

rows.question: Find all photometrically observable Galaxy that have spectral observations. Retrieve the object id, right ascension, and declination.
rows.pred_sql:
WITH photoobj_canonical_coords_and_type AS (
  SELECT
    p.objid AS objid,
    p.ra AS ra,
    p.dec AS dec,
    p.type AS type
  FROM photoobj p
),
specobj_core_links AS (
  SELECT
    s.specobjid AS specobjid,
    s.bestobjid AS bestobjid
  FROM specobj s
),
photoobj_with_any_spectrum_match AS (
  SELECT
    p.objid AS objid,
    p.ra AS ra,
    p.dec AS dec,
    p.type AS type,
    CASE WHEN (s_best.specobjid IS NOT NULL OR s_direct.specobjid IS NOT NULL) THEN true ELSE false END AS has_spectrum,
    COALESCE(s_direct.specobjid, s_best.specobjid) AS matched_specobjid,
    COALESCE(s_direct.bestobjid, s_best.bestobjid) AS matched_bestobjid
  FROM photoobj_canonical_coords_and_type p
  LEFT JOIN specobj_core_links s_best
    ON s_best.bestobjid = p.objid
  LEFT JOIN specobj_core_links s_direct
    ON s_direct.specobjid = p.objid
)
SELECT p.objid AS objid,
       p.ra AS ra,
       p.dec AS dec
FROM photoobj_canonical_coords_and_type p
JOIN photoobj_with_any_spectrum_match s ON s.objid = p.objid
JOIN photo_type t ON t.value = p.type
WHERE s.has_spectrum
  AND p.ra IS NOT NULL
  AND p.dec IS NOT NULL
  AND (t.name ILIKE '%Galaxy%' OR t.description ILIKE '%Galaxy%')
ORDER BY p.objid
